rationale: Attempt-00 selected (block_M=128, block_N=64, block_K=64, num_stages=1) with proxy_cost 2.377, actual smem 32768 bytes (= cap), 126 registers, compiled and numerically passed on the exact source/TIR, simulated_us 157.05 (GB10 simulator estimate, not hardware; no CUDA binary executed). Domains kept full so HiGHS still owns tuple selection: block_M divides 128, block_N and block_K divide 4096, threads fixed at 128 per allowed domain. Shared-memory cap retained at 32768 (the portability cap) because actual compiled smem already hit it and larger caps risk Metal portability; the 4*block_M*block_N epilogue term plus the hard 32768 portability cap jointly constrain large-tile choices. Weight revision: the stage-1 choice leaves pipeline unresolved, so pipeline is raised to 2 to favor more stages (multi-stage pipelining tends to shorten K-loop stalls); traffic is raised to 1.5 since the wide-M, tall-N shape keeps traffic reductions valuable; launches is lowered to 0.5 because the current tiling already yields modest launch counts relative to traffic/footprint; footprint stays at 1 to keep pressure off the 32768 cap. Since only attempt-00 exists, exclusion is not yet needed and all tuples remain eligible; HiGHS explores unmeasured points rather than measured enumeration. Next hypothesis: with pipeline weight increased, a (block_M=64 or 128, block_N=64, block_K=32, num_stages=2 or 3) tuple with the same or smaller footprint may lower the analytic proxy while compiling under the cap and passing numerical checks; verify Metal-executed source/TIR validity and treat GB10 simulated_us as ranking proxy only, not hardware latency, and do not claim global optimality.
